cards.intuition: Near-identical chunks are duplicate passengers consuming scarce seats. Keep one representative or merge adjacent spans so another source can contribute evidence.
cards.formula: deduplicate by source position, text overlap, or embedding similarity

cards.intuition: Choose a candidate that answers the query without merely repeating what is already selected. Lambda controls the pull between direct relevance and useful novelty.
cards.formula: MMR(d) = lambda × sim(q,d) - (1-lambda) × max sim(d,s) for selected s

cards.intuition: Long-context models often use evidence at the beginning or end better than evidence buried centrally. Put strongest evidence at an edge and preserve coherent source order.
cards.formula: long-context accuracy often follows a U-shaped position curve

cards.intuition: Give each chunk a stable label mapped back to its document and offsets. The answer's marker then becomes a real pointer rather than decorative punctuation.
cards.formula: source label → document + chunk + character offsets
cards.topic: Citation-Grounded Extraction: Attributing Spans to Sources

cards.intuition: Exact or normalized matching proves the quoted words exist in the cited chunk and catches fabricated quotations. A separate entailment check must decide whether they support the claim.
cards.formula: quote existence is not claim support
cards.topic: Citation-Grounded Extraction: Attributing Spans to Sources

cards.concept: Why sentence-level citation is the useful grain
cards.intuition: It lets a reader test each claim against a source without the noise of word-level labels or the ambiguity of one source list for an entire answer.
cards.topic: Citation-Grounded Extraction: Attributing Spans to Sources

cards.intuition: Pre-filtering searches only allowed candidates. Post-filtering throws away disallowed hits after ranking and can starve the prompt unless you overfetch.
cards.formula: post-filter fetch target ≈ desired k / expected pass rate

cards.intuition: When inferred constraints yield too few results, relax the least trustworthy inference first and disclose it. Never relax authorization or tenant boundaries.
cards.formula: relax inferred filters before explicit constraints; never relax security defaults

cards.intuition: A filter treats missing labels like failures, so enforcing a sparsely populated field can make valid documents invisible. Audit coverage before making it mandatory.
cards.formula: unlabeled document + enforced field filter = excluded document

cards.intuition: A compact prompt rich in useful evidence beats a large prompt carrying the same evidence plus noise. Extra tokens can distract the model while increasing cost and latency.
cards.formula: relevance density = useful context tokens / total context tokens
cards.topic: Context Window Budgeting: Relevance Density over Volume

cards.intuition: The window is shared by instructions, history, question, evidence, and answer reserve. What remains is a maximum, not an obligation to add weak chunks.
cards.formula: context ceiling = window - system - history - question - answer reserve
cards.topic: Context Window Budgeting: Relevance Density over Volume

cards.intuition: Admit candidates while evidence stays strong, then stop when scores collapse. Fixed-k padding turns low-score tail items into model-visible distractors.
cards.formula: stop at relevance threshold or score cliff, before the token ceiling
cards.topic: Context Window Budgeting: Relevance Density over Volume
